Koine genomic fourth opinion (REML lens via sommer)

Source: R/koine_genomic.R
koine_genomic_lens.Rd

Fit the established REML genomic BLUP with sommer on the same data and return a genomic lens: the field-standard fourth opinion to set beside the Bayesian multi-backend answer. (triangulate_genomic(), which compared the two, was removed from flexyBayes in version 0.14.0.) The lens carries the REML heritability, variance components (with standard errors), and breeding values (named by genotype, aligning to the flexyBayes GEBVs), so divergence between the Bayesian and REML answers is surfaced rather than hidden.

Usage

koine_genomic_lens(fixed, data, K, geno = "geno")

Arguments

fixed

A fixed-effect formula, e.g. y ~ 1 or y ~ env.

data

A data frame with the response, fixed effects, and the genotype factor; one or more records per genotype.

K

The genomic (or pedigree) relationship matrix; its row / column names are the genotype levels and must cover the genotypes in data.

geno

The genotype grouping-factor column name (default "geno").

Value

A genomic lens: list(h2, var_g, var_e, gebv, label), where h2 / var_g / var_e are list(estimate, se) (the heritability SE is a delta-method approximation) and gebv is a named numeric vector of REML breeding values.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bayes_fit <- flexyBayes::flexybayes(
  y ~ 1, random = ~ vm(geno, G), data = dat,
  known_matrices = list(G = G), backend = "greta"
)
koine <- koine_genomic_lens(y ~ 1, dat, G, geno = "geno")
koine$h2
head(koine$gebv)
} # }
